lithos_version: lithos 0.5.0 @ a4d2d62; every error envelope below probed against a live Lithos (MCP serverInfo 3.2.0, 2026-10-04) except where observed_divergences says otherwise

request.notes: The whole request surface: a terminal (completed/cancelled) task back to `open`. Clears `resolved_at` and `outcome`, records the reopen as a `[Reopened]` finding (the only surviving evidence of the prior outcome — see tasks.REOPENED_FINDING_PREFIX) and emits `task.reopened`. An already-open task is `task_not_resolved`, a missing one `task_not_found`. Every id goes through the SHARED resolver, whose whole domain is probed: a full id (>= 36 characters, a UUID) is handed straight to this tool's own lookup; anything shorter than SIX characters that is not an exact id is `invalid_input`; a 6-to-35-character value is searched as a PREFIX, and matching nothing is the resolver's own `task_not_found` ("No task matches id prefix …", a different message from this tool's own not-found, same code) while matching several is `ambiguous_id_prefix` with up to FIVE `{id, title}` candidate RECORDS — the message states the capped count. Lens sends a full id for this tool (the funnel acts on a task it has just read), so none of the prefix refusals is on a Lens request; all are vendored because the mapper must still answer them.

errors.message: Task 'influx-gate-human' is already open; nothing to reopen.
task_id 'infl' is too short: pass the full task id or a prefix of at least 6 characters.
Task id prefix '506155' (task_id) is ambiguous: 2 or more matches. Retry with a longer prefix or a full id from candidates.

observed_divergences: `reblocked` is a list of task IDS, not records, and is non-empty ONLY when a *completed* blocker or gate is reopened: reopening a CANCELLED task un-strands its dependents (they were `blocker_unsatisfiable`, not ready) and re-blocks nobody — the `cancelled_reopen` variant. That is why T3 D8 counts the cancelled case from the task's own active outgoing dependency edges instead. The success payload is transcribed from the documented return (the quoted `{success, reblocked}` "plus the resolved task_id + title and the new updated_at") — it cannot be probed without reopening a real task. The `task_not_resolved` envelope IS probed (reopening an OPEN task is refused, so the probe writes nothing): an earlier pass of this slice had composed it as "… is not resolved (status: open).", which the server never says. Its code is what the mapper reads. Probed 2026-10-04 against the live Lithos this environment reaches (MCP serverInfo 3.2.0). That server is NEWER than a4d2d62 — it serves `lithos_task_edge_delete`, which lithos-core `bd66d57c` added after 0.5.0 — and the Lithos source itself could not be read from this build environment, so where a message below is marked probed it is the live server's text, with ids substituted; a reviewer holding the a4d2d62 source should record any wording that differs there as a divergence here rather than replace the probed text.
